story.head: Marner’s favorite opponent
paras: The Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Friday, while the Bruins (10-4-1) beat Chicago 5-4 in overtime on Saturday. Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Bruins first in the Atlantic (fourth).

The Golden Knights have played better than their record (.633) says: their chances are worth about .691, and their goaltending has held them back. The Bruins’ record (.700) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.552), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), but have had shaky goaltending (31st). The Bruins, by contrast, have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (2nd lowest). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest), so the Golden Knights’ defensemen shoot a lot, and theirs not so much. Boston has allowed 2.40 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. The Bruins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Golden Knights.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Boston. Mark Stone (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Bruins, David Pastrňák (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Vegas.

Jeremy Swayman (7-3-1 / .912 SV% in 11 GS) has been terrific for Boston and will likely start. Vegas has two options in net: Adin Hill (5-2-0 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) and Carter Hart (4-3-1 / .889 SV% in 8 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Hill got the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net. Swayman has a .875 save percentage in five starts against the Golden Knights, well under his usual .906. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Marco Sturm likes to send Mittelstadt, Lindholm and Hagens out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Barbashev, Eichel and Stone.
